title: Adaptive backpressure & fallback orchestration for regional/tier routing
creator: Olivia Chen
description: Goal: Implement an adaptive backpressure and automatic fallback orchestration layer that triggers when per-route and per-region service degradation is detected. This ticket covers the trigger heuristics (429 bursts, sustained timeouts, error-rate thresholds, p95/p99 latency windows), the local circuit-breaker state machine, and the automated decision logic to pick fallback model variants (smaller/quantized, regional fallback, tier downgrade) while tracking quality/regression signals.
acceptance_criteria: 1) System raises fallback decision event when any configured threshold is breached (429 spike, 5 consecutive timeouts, or error-rate > 5% over rolling 60s).
2) Circuit breaker transitions (CLOSED/OPEN/HALF-OPEN) correctly for a route and prevents additional requests from hitting degraded pool for configured cooldown.
3) Fallback decision chooses allowed variant per route policy (ordered list) and logs a decision with metadata (reason, metric snapshot, selected variant).
4) Observability: dashboard shows fallback events, per-route failure taxonomy, and downstream quality regressions vs baseline prompt set.
5) End-to-end integration test against local inference emulator and chaos harness demonstrates successful failover without user-facing 5xxs for >95% of requests.
design_notes: We will implement a two-layer approach: (A) detection: short and long windows for 429s, timeouts, and error-rate using exponential weighted moving averages and simple counters; (B) decision + action: per-route circuit breakers with dynamic cooldowns and a fallback policy engine that evaluates candidate variants by priority, compatibility (max tokens, functions support), and quality budget. Circuit breaker states follow the standard CLOSED -> OPEN -> HALF-OPEN with dynamically sized OPEN windows (base_cooldown * severity_multiplier). Severity is computed from combined normalized signals (rate of 429s, p95 increase, consecutive timeouts). To avoid oscillation when dropping to smaller variants, we inject a probation window for HALF-OPEN where a small sample of traffic (5%) probes the primary model.
tradeoffs:
- Aggressive fallbacks reduce user-facing errors but increase risk of quality regressions (hallucination, shorter answers).
- Larger cooldowns reduce flapping but increase time on suboptimal models.
- More complex heuristics require tuning and add CPU memory to router service.
- Regional failover can increase latency for some users but preserves availability.
metric_targets: Primary: reduce 5xx user-facing errors by 80% during degraded pool events. Secondary: maintain mean quality score drop < 10% (measured by eval prompts). Operational: reduction in repeated retries from client side by 60% within the same minute.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Instrument detection signals in router service (429 counters, timeout counters, p95/p99 latency windows) and expose as metrics (prometheus) - done (ENG-33112). Phase 2: Implement local circuit-breaker module with state persisted in redis and expose transition events to eventbus - in progress. Phase 3: Build fallback policy engine that reads per-route policies from config store and executes model variant selection. Phase 4: Integrate with rollout API to execute canary probe traffic during HALF-OPEN. Phase 5: Run chaos/soak test in staging with synthetic load and compare quality/regression dashboards. Phase 6: Gradual prod rollout by % traffic over 3 days.
progress_updates: 2026-02-18: Kickoff meeting with runtime, router, and console teams. Agreed on primary signals and the need for a probation probing window for HALF-OPEN state.
2026-02-24: Router team merged metrics PR for 429/timeouts/p95 (GH: github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/512). Added labels for per-route thresholds in config store.

2026-02-28: Prototype circuit-breaker state machine implemented; working locally using redis for state. Observed initial oscillation in staging under synthetic burst test; mitigated by adding exponential backoff to cooldown calculation.

2026-03-03: Design review notes from PM (Luis Martin): require explicit policy to opt routes into regional fallback. Also requested a simple `quality_budget` parameter on route policy so Product can control acceptable regressions.
open_questions: What are sensible defaults for thresholds (429 rate per minute, consecutive timeouts) for free-tier vs enterprise-tier customers?
Should regional fallback be disabled for privacy-restricted routes by default (yes for now per PM)?
How will we surface model quality regressions in the Console so owners can quickly rollback fallback policies?
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for state transitions and cooldown math. 2) Integration test against the inference emulator simulating: 429 flood, backend timeouts, and large p95 shift. 3) Staging chaos test: cross-region outage, emulated GPU OOMs causing elevated timeouts. 4) Regression evaluation suite runs on baseline and fallback variants to quantify quality drop.
rollback_plan: If fallback causes >20% user-visible quality regression or unexpected latency increases beyond SLA, we will: (1) automatically revert fallback decisions for affected routes via console toggle, (2) disable regional fallback globally for that release, (3) revert router binary to previous stable if necessary.
